title: What is the 'My Moon My Man' trend? TikTok's couples slideshow
answer: The "My Moon My Man" trend is a TikTok couples slideshow that took off in November 2026: a selfie first, then a photo with a partner, set to FINNEAS's cover of Feist's 2007 song "My Moon My Man," with a caption that seems to continue across the swipe.
body:
The format is short and simple. The first slide is usually a solo selfie with the caption "my moon my maaa..." stretched out to the edge, and the second slide reveals a photo with a boyfriend, girlfriend or spouse, so the words appear to finish on the next picture. The sound is a slow, stripped-down cover by FINNEAS rather than Feist's upbeat original. Many people play it straight as a sweet reveal; others turn it into a joke, swapping the partner photo for a pet, a snack or a partner caught mid-fall.

Feist released "My Moon My Man" in 2007 on her album The Reminder. FINNEAS performed his version in September 2026, when Feist was inducted into the Canadian Songwriters Hall of Fame in Toronto, and it was first released as an Amazon Music exclusive. Know Your Meme traces the couples format with his cover to Nov. 7, 2026; a post on Nov. 9 passed 1.6 million likes, and versions spread to Instagram and Facebook within about a week. An earlier version of the slideshow, set to Feist's original, had appeared in September with little attention.

The trend pushed the sound to No. 1 on TikTok's global trending audio chart, and FINNEAS put the cover on all major streaming services around Nov. 20. Billboard data cited by music outlets showed streams of both his cover and Feist's original jumping in mid-November. The song had already enjoyed a revival after it played in an episode of the Canadian series Heated Rivalry in late 2025, so many viewers recognized it.

For parents and teachers: the trend is wholesome, a way to show off a relationship or a friendship. The only thing worth a quick word is privacy: a couples slideshow puts a second person's face online, so it is fair to ask that person first.

faq.a: The version with FINNEAS's cover took off on TikTok on Nov. 7, 2026, and peaked in mid-November.
